title: Office — LibreOffice files lose some formatting when saved

steps.path: Saving a LibreOffice document (.odt, .ods, .odp) in Office
steps.headline: LibreOffice documents gain unwanted bold when saved. How should Office handle saving them?
steps.today: You chose to include LibreOffice files in the first version. In testing, a real LibreOffice memo opened perfectly, but after one save, bulleted lines that were only partly bold came back fully bold (659 bold characters became 1,180).
steps.problem: The fault is in the file translator every OnlyOffice-based editor uses, including OnlyOffice's own newest version, so no choice of editor avoids it. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files are not affected.
steps.proposal: Three ways to handle it. Opening and reading LibreOffice files stays in the first version in all three.

options.label: Save a Word copy
options.summary: Editing a LibreOffice file saves your changes to a Word/Excel/PowerPoint copy beside it; the original is never rewritten.
pros: Nothing in the original file is ever damaged.
The copy keeps its formatting exactly, from then on.
cons: You end up with two files, and LibreOffice users you share with get a Word file.

options.label: Save, with a warning
options.summary: Office saves back to the LibreOffice file, after a one-time warning that some formatting may change.
pros: One file, in the format it came in.
cons: The formatting drift still happens when it happens.
Easy to click past a warning and only notice later.

options.label: Open read-only
options.summary: LibreOffice files open for reading only until the translator is fixed; Office offers "Save as Word copy" if you want to edit.
pros: Clearest: nothing changes a LibreOffice file.
cons: An extra step before editing any LibreOffice file.

steps.path: Euro-Office's public issue tracker on GitHub
steps.headline: Should I report this bug publicly to the Euro-Office project, under your GitHub account?
steps.today: The bug is in Euro-Office's translator (and OnlyOffice's). Nobody seems to have reported it for this case yet.
steps.problem: A public report is the only way it gets fixed upstream, but it is posted under your name and cannot be fully taken back.
steps.proposal: Yes: I post a short report with the steps and the bold counts, using neutral test files only — never your documents. No: nothing is posted.
